body.atext: In this paper, we have decomposed the velocity components in CO rovibrational absorption lines (v = 0 → 1, ΔJ = ±1, λ ∼ 4.67 μm) in two AGNs (IR01250, IR08572 NW) and two AGN-starburst composites (U5101, N4418) using high-resolution (R ∼ 5000–10,000) spectroscopy to probe the spatial distributions and determine the dynamical and physical properties of clumps inside the molecular torus. Our findings in this paper are summarized as follows:1.We have decomposed discrete velocity components with multiple LOS velocities, velocity dispersions, and excitation states in each CO rovibrational absorption transition for all targets. From the velocity decompositions, we have detected two or more velocity components, i.e., (a) and (b) in IR01250, U5101, and N4418, and (a)–(c) in IR08572 NW, associated with the molecular torus.i.Component (a) is outflowing with the high LOS velocity ∣V LOS∣ ∼ 160–240 km s−1, and it has the largest velocity dispersion σ V ∼ 130–180 km s−1 in all objects other than N4418. In N4418, component (a) also has the largest velocity dispersion, σ V ∼140 km s−1, but it has a systemic LOS velocity. In addition, component (a) is detected up to high rotational levels with J ∼ 20–40 in all targets.ii.Component (b) is also outflowing with the high LOS velocity ∣V LOS∣ ≳ 80 km s−1 in IR01250 and IR08572 NW. On the other hand, component (b) is systemic or inflowing with the low LOS velocity ∣V LOS∣ ≲ 30 km s−1 in U5101 and N4418. Moreover, this component has the velocity dispersion σ V ∼ 50–80 km s−1, which is smaller than that of component (a) in all objects. Although these components are also detected up to high rotational levels with J ∼ 10–30, the highest rotational level is lower than that of component (a) in each target.iii.Component (c) of IR08572 NW is inflowing with the LOS velocity V LOS ∼ 100 km s−1 and the velocity dispersion σ V ∼ 40 km s−1, and it is highly excited up to J ∼ 26. 2.The detection of multiple distinct velocity components in the torus indicates that the torus medium is a clumpy medium and that the clumps form multiple clusters in separated spatial regions in the torus of each object.3.Assuming that the radius of rotation of each velocity component is related to its velocity dispersion as Rrot∝σV−2 , we estimate the ratio of the radius of rotation for each velocity component to that of component (a), which has the largest velocity dispersion and is probably located in the innermost region of the torus. As a result, component (b) in IR08572 NW and in IR01250 is outflowing in the outer region of the torus, with the ratio R rot,b/R rot,a ∼ 5–13. On the other hand, component (b) in U5101 and N4418 is systemic or inflowing in more compact regions with the ratios with R rot,b/R rot,a ∼ 2–5. In addition, component (c) in IR08572 NW is inflowing in the outermost region with R rot,c/R rot,a ∼ 17.4.These results indicate the dynamical structure of IR08572 NW and IR01250, where clumps outflow in inner regions of the torus (outflow-dominant regions), with R rot/R rot,a ∼ 5–13 and inflow in outer regions with R rot/R rot,a ∼ 17 (Figure 9). On the other hand, the radius of the outflow-dominant region is more compact in U5101 with R rot/R rot,a ∼ 2 and is nonexistent in N4418, where outflowing clumps are not detected even in the vicinity of the AGN core. Accordingly, we conclude that the molecular torus has a dynamic inner structure with outflows and inflows rather than a static structure.5.The radiation-driven fountain model (K. Wada et al. 2016) can naturally explain both LOS velocities ∣V LOS∣ ≲ 240 km s−1 and the locations of the innermost component (a). On the other hand, another model may be necessary to describe the inflow, apart from the equatorial disk, in order to reproduce the inflowing components in IR08572 NW and U5101.6.We have estimated the physical properties of each velocity component based on the level populations and the non-LTE model, RADEX:i.The innermost component (a), which is detected in all objects, is attributable to hot (T kin ≳ 550) and dense ( log(nH2/cm−3)≳6 ) clumps. In addition, this component covers more than ∼30% of the NIR continuum source, which is expected to be the dust-sublimation layer with a radius of ≲1 pc, and has the large CO column density N CO ∼ 1018.7–19.3 cm−2.ii.On the other hand, the outer component (b) is attributable to colder (T kin ≲ 30–140 K) and less dense ( log(nH2/cm−3)∼5.6–6.5 ) clumps than those of component (a). Component (b) also covers the NIR continuum source, with a large covering factor ≳60%. In addition, component (b) is likely illuminated by an FIR-to-(sub)millimeter background higher than T bg ∼ 20–400 K.In conclusion, we have observationally found that the inner structure of the molecular torus in each of the four targets we have studied has a dynamic structure containing outflowing and inflowing clumps. We have also found that the clumps inside the torus are collisionally excited in the innermost regions, whereas they are radiationally excited by the FIR-to-(sub)millimeter background in the outer regions.
